senses.sense_definition: To act in an excessively submissive manner; to grovel or show unwarranted deference to someone.

examples.text: The manager refused to <w>kowtow</w> to the demands of the aggressive investors.
She was not the kind of politician who would <w>kowtow</w> to party leaders just to keep her job.

senses.sense_definition: To kneel and bow low enough to touch one's forehead to the ground, especially as a traditional gesture of respect.

examples.text: Subjects were required to <w>kowtow</w> before the imperial throne during formal audiences.
The monk would <w>kowtow</w> repeatedly in prayer before entering the temple shrine.

senses.sense_definition: An act of kneeling and touching the forehead to the ground, or a subservient gesture of submission.

examples.text: The elders performed a formal <w>kowtow</w> in front of the ancestral shrine.
He refused to offer a humiliating <w>kowtow</w> simply to secure political favors.
